blocks.content: These one-liners cover GDP concepts, inflation types, banking tools, fiscal indicators, external sector basics, human development measures and planning facts commonly asked in RRB exams.
NATIONAL INCOME

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: National Income accounts track total economic production and income generated across primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors.
Inflation management involves monitoring Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Wholesale Price Index (WPI) metrics.
Banking & Monetary Policy regulates liquidity, credit availability, and interest rates through the Reserve Bank of India.
Fiscal Policy governs public finance, tax structures, deficit financing, and budgetary allocations.
External Sector metrics monitor Balance of Payments (BoP), foreign exchange reserves, and trade balances.
Planning & Human Development evaluate welfare metrics, HDI rankings, and long-term socio-economic strategies.

blocks.content: • GDP measures total value of final goods and services produced within domestic territory.
• GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA).
• NDP = GDP – Depreciation.
• NNP at factor cost is called National Income.
• Nominal GDP is measured at current prices.
• Real GDP is measured at constant prices.
• GVA = GDP – Net Indirect Taxes.
• Base Year for GDP calculation in India is 2011-12.
• CSO is now part of NSO (National Statistical Office).
INFLATION
• CPI measures retail inflation.
• WPI measures wholesale inflation.
• Core inflation excludes food and fuel.
• Headline inflation includes all items.
• Demand-pull inflation is caused by excess demand.
• Cost-push inflation is caused by rising production costs.
• Stagflation = High inflation + High unemployment.
• Deflation = Persistent fall in general price level.
BANKING & MONETARY POLICY
• RBI established in 1935.
CHAPTER 15 : ECONOMY ONE-LINERS
• Repo rate is the policy rate of RBI.
• Reverse repo rate is rate at which RBI absorbs liquidity.
• CRR is percentage of deposits kept with RBI in cash.
• SLR is percentage kept in liquid assets.
• MSF is emergency borrowing facility for banks.
• LAF stands for Liquidity Adjustment Facility.
• Open Market Operations involve buying/selling government securities.
FISCAL POLICY
• Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure – Total receipts (excluding borrowings).
• Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure – Revenue receipts.
• Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit – Interest payments.

blocks.content: • FRBM Act enacted in 2003.
• GST implemented on 1 July 2017.
• GST is destination-based indirect tax.
• Progressive tax rate increases with income.
EXTERNAL SECTOR
• BoP has Current Account and Capital Account.
• Current Account Deficit occurs when imports exceed exports.
• India follows managed floating exchange rate.
• Forex reserves maintained by RBI.
• Depreciation makes exports cheaper.
• Appreciation makes imports cheaper.
HUMAN DEVELOPMENT
• HDI published by UNDP.
• HDI components: Health, Education, Income.
• MPI measures multidimensional poverty.

items: Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) targets headline inflation based on the CPI (Combined) index.
Gross Domestic Product at Market Price includes Net Indirect Taxes added to GDP at Factor Cost.
Important banking ratios like Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) and Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) are crucial quantitative instruments of RBI.

blocks.content: • Demographic dividend arises from large working-age population.
PLANNING & DEVELOPMENT
• First Five-Year Plan focused on agriculture.
• Second Five-Year Plan based on Mahalanobis model.
• Green Revolution began during Plan Holiday (1966-69).
• NITI Aayog replaced Planning Commission in 2015.
IMPORTANT RATIOS
• Tax-to-GDP ratio measures fiscal capacity.
• Debt-to-GDP ratio measures debt sustainability.
• Gini coefficient measures income inequality.
